problem:
Consider the system of linear equations given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}3x+\sqrt{7}y=0.3 \\ -2\sqrt{0.1}x+3y=\sqrt{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the system has exactly one solution, which of the following statements are true?

- The lines $3x+\sqrt{7}y=0.3$ and $-2\sqrt{0.1}x+3y=\sqrt{7}$ intersect exactly at one point
- The determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $0$
- The coefficient matrix is invertible

activity_context.topic_title: The Invertible Matrix Theorem in Terms of 2x2 Systems of Equations

feedback.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations given by

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-2y=-1 \\ 3y-x=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the system has exactly one solution, which of the following statements are true?

- The lines $2x-2y=-1$ and $3y-x=1$ intersect at infinitely many  points
- The coefficient matrix is not  invertible
- The determinant of the coefficient matrix is not equal to zero
feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that given $A=[\begin{aligned}{a}_{11} & {a}_{12} \\ {a}_{21} & {a}_{22}\end{aligned}]$, then according to the invertible matrix theorem the following statements are equivalent:    

- $A$ is invertible.

- The system $Ax=b$ has exactly one solution for any $2\times 1$ column vector $b.$

- The system $Ax=0$ has the unique zero solution.

- The lines ${a}_{11}x+{a}_{12}y={b}_{1}$ and ${a}_{21}x+{a}_{22}y={b}_{2}$ intersect at exactly one point.

- $det(A)\ne 0.$

Also, we are told that the second part of the invertible matrix theorem is true. So, all the other parts of the theorem are true too. Therefore, according to the theorem:

- Statement I is false by the fourth part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement II is false by the first part of the invertible matrix theorem.

- Statement III is true by the fifth part of the invertible matrix theorem.

Therefore, only statement III is true.
